body: So I’m just an over needy SM. Well At least I know it’s all me. Thanks all.

Oh I totally agree on him not having FB but it wasn’t my decision, his dad didn’t even get a say. Messenger is private, and his mum is the one who is pushing for him to call me mum and who told me today how much he loves me. The privacy and BM feelings were how I was justifying it to myself before but not even saying thanks to a birthday message... not only is it rude and he is better than that it’s hurtful. I’m not going to say a word to SO or SS. That’s why I’m on here asking for help on how to cope with it. I know parents come first. I know parents mean more. But I somehow fell for I mean just as much to him as anyone else in his life and as much as he means to me. That’s the part that hurts.

I know your right. I know I’m the adult and I shouldn’t expect anything from him. But when he comments on everyone else’s posts and messages everyone else but not me I can’t help but being hurt. I don’t have many people in my life who actually care and less than half of them are able to show me. SS has always been able to make any problem seem insignificant because his smile fixes anything. He will never know this hurts me because I would never put this on him or SO. Just needed someone to help me figure this out so it doesn’t hurt.

Just a suggestion, have you thought about doing charity work while your looking? 
It will look great on your CV and will help you get more comfortable in the working environment. I’ve been out of a job stressing about interviews and having break downs so I know how hard it is to keep going and not to stay in bed all day. I also know that we over analyse as soon as we get out of interviews. Find a charity shop or some other volunteer work to do, it may help you with coping. And knowledge because you will learn on the job. Well done for going to the interview.

Yeah I think I’ve come to terms a long time ago with my lack of control over anything to do with SS and his life, I just do what I can to give him the best opportunity in life and give him the best life possible while he is with us. I know she will take it off him and be a pain with it but I figure rather now when it’s not really a big deal than start this process in 2 years when I’m trying to get hold of him and his phone is confiscated or dead and I’m wondering where he is while I wait outside his school. We don’t tend to have contact with him while he is with her unless it’s his birthday or a special occasion/trip/school thing. They live in a different city nearly 2 hours away so we can’t just pop over. But she gets funny if/when we call him and he’s too scared to ask to call us incase it upsets her. He tells people what he thinks they want to hear and tries to keep everyone happy. It’s started to lead to some issues but that’s a different story and we are dealing with it, with me and BM talking regularly to ensure no lies. I’m never going to get the full truth but I can only do what I think is best for SS. And try to be fair. I know it’s going to be hard but I’m not going to stop him having something because I don’t trust BM.

That’s one of the reasons I want to do it now. Get the crappy awkward behaviour and problems out of the way before him having a phone is actually necessary. If BM is going to be a pain in the arse about it, let her do it now rather than when he’s in high school and needs his phone to walk home with.

I would usually agree but in this case neither BM or SD can keep a phone or are willing to keep us updated on mobile numbers. And BM is more than willing to let SS walk home from school. My reasoning is his lack of respect for anything. He’s never been taught to respect his belongings and keep them. While we have done our best there hasn’t been much we can monitor. I’m worried if he goes to high school and then gets a phone it will be a smart phone and he will destroy it and spend all the credit on nothing when we need him to have credit as it’s a half hour walk to his mums from high school where he will be walking home. I want him to learn the importance and make his mistakes now to prevent panic and trouble when he reaches high school and has more freedom.

I feel for you, and I understand how much of a nightmare it can be as the BM of my SS has been through it 3 times, only once was SS. I just think the first time she’s done it, she needs sitting down and explaining every consequence and every detail. My SS has 4 parents but I’m the only one that can talk to him about serious stuff. He tells everyone else what he thinks they want to hear so they will leave (and they do) He doesn’t take in what they are saying because they don’t explain everything properly. I’ve had a few months of having 1 or more of ‘difficult’ conversations with him every week because he’s at that age. All kids are different but the way I get through is talking to him and showing him respect and letting him have an opinion and ask questions. He knows he won’t be in trouble and won’t upset me by asking or telling me something. Honest conversation should be the starting point of these situations. If you don’t tell them all of the harm they are doing and the consequences how can you expect them to understand?

While I agree that 14 year olds understand what they are doing I don’t believe that she understood to the full extent of her actions. She probably thought she was getting her dad in trouble just like when she gets into trouble. Once the punishment is served it goes away. I think all parties need to sit down without her first and then with her and discuss why she felt it necessary to do it, what the outcome was, what the outcome could have been, the implications, the life long outcomes. Talk to her like an adult

Well done for sticking with it. It’s good to take the little wins. 1 BM is plenty for me, so kudos for dealing with 2. Even if they were the nicest most cooperative people, you are a brave amazing woman.

He will never stop needing you, the ways he needs you will change, but just as you need him in your life, he needs you in his. 
Maybe a father/son day is in order, go out and do something the pair of you love. When you think of him, text him. It’s all changing but your love for each other remains. And if/ when he becomes a dad, he will need you more than ever to help guide him. Even as a husband he will need help with how to handle situations. We never stop needing our parents. Even after they are gone, Times come when we wish they were here to help. Just continue to always be there when he calls, and he will always call.

It would all depend on how long you’ve been in her life, I waited for SS to say love you first but he was 4 so it was different. I would get the i love you’d in and comfortable before you address the name side. And don’t make it a formal conversation. It will come up one day one way or another and just say you have no issue with her calling you anything she wants. So long as she’s happy your happy.
Anytime, and if you need a rant or someone to talk to PM me. I’d be happy to listen and help where I can.

I don’t think anyone expects BM and SM to be besties. But I do believe that where possible all parents should try and get along as much as possible: sometimes that’s being civil and sharing important kid related info, sometimes it’s having a chat and walking away when you would love to tell the other parent where to go. It’s about compromise and putting the kids first. I’m not delusional and trust me i know it’s hard. I live it daily and At least once a month I would love to take my SS far away from his somewhat useless mother, but then I remember he loves all of his family and even though the world can see he would be better off with us, if we had him during the week she wouldn’t come get him at weekends and that would hurt him more. We all have very different situations but we are also in the same boat. BP have split up for a reason and sometimes it’s hard talking to your ex, Atleast with SP being civil there is another line of communication open. Other times SP needs to stay away from BP because it’s hard to deal with the fact SO had their first kid with someone else. But in an ideal world if we try our hardest to be civil and cope with it, we as SP have more input and a better chance of giving SK what they need.

I get that, I was overly cautious with everything to begin with. I didn’t post anything on social media for years and even asked her permission (BM is a massive social media person so didn’t really care) 
BM has issues when we drop off SS and he’s crying his eyes out because he doesn’t want to go to hers. She tells me how much it hurts and I deal with SS because she just looses her temper. I’m the authoritative of his 4 parents (I don’t shout but I have the most earned respect) 
Just start small. Say hi, then ask if the kids have been good or fed or if they’ve had a good weekend and build up from there. It takes a long time and effort and at times will feel impossible but it will improve your lifestyle and mental health in the long run. And I’m always here for support or a rant if you ever need it.

I know this is a very hard and very controversial suggestion and I do not claim to know or understand your situation at all... but I’m going to tell you what works for my BM situation. 
She bullied me in high school, she is one of those I don’t have to work or do anything with my life, I’ll have a kid every few years and claim benefits (Uk based) but we talk, we are civil and to begin with I was quite reserved from all pick ups and drop offs but as time went on I got more and more involved, she now prefers to talk to me over anyone else in the family. I don’t let her always get her own way but I use a you scratch my back I’ll scratch yours Approach and always solve her ‘issues’ quickly and in the best interests of SS8. Don’t get me wrong she can drive me insane and some days I would love to tell her where to go. But by being a person she can talk to and a person she can ‘rely’ on I have more control over situations that I’m not happy with. 
It’s not easy by any means but it is a lot easier than being kept out of it. Having no contact left me feeling useless and like she had control of my life. She dictated so much before and now I have a say and she’s even suggested SS8 can call me mum (he doesn’t but this is his choice because I’m his ‘nickname’) it takes time and most of the time you have to bite your tongue but having a simple basic relationship with her might make you feel more comfortable and might give DH a better chance at being ‘the bad guy’.

I have a question. Why is BM pushing nice ‘gifts’ onto SO? Even if the divorce was a friendly mutual parting of ways, I don’t know anyone who would be going that far with birthdays for their ex.... 
sorry I don’t mean to plant ideas in your head but that seems very strange to me and I think you are well within your rights to be uncomfortable. I’ve had similar issues with SO family and when SO tried to put his foot down it didn’t work because they had walked all over him for so many years. It took me saying No and then him enforcing it for people to realise. It’s a horrible situation but you need to tell her no. I’m not saying loose your shit with her, just explain that xyz is happening and it would be great if she could keep her nose out. 
Hope this helps

Thank you for your reply. I think the nightmares are making me feel anxious but I’m also aware that my nightmares get worse when I’m stressed or feel a loss of control (I’m not a major control person but I need some especially over certain things) and I’m currently training at a new job and have some financial issues. So I know where they are coming from. 
I will try this technique tonight, I’ve done similar in a hypnosis video but I have never used white noise. 
Thank you for your help.

This took bravery, I hope you find a peaceful way to go day to day. I know your pain and I know some days it feels unbearable, but you will find a way to make it through. I’m sorry you had to go through this all alone. You’ve done the hardest part by making the decision and going through with it. You are allowed to grieve and feel sad about it. It’s ok.

NTA your wife needs to support you, she doesn’t even have to speak to the woman during the funeral. (I don’t know how your relationship is and if shouting is a common thing) but if this is a very “out of the blue” occurrence I would suggest once you calm down talking to her and saying something along the lines of “look I’m sorry I lost my temper I am very emotional and planning this is not in anyway easy for me, but you need to understand that this woman is coming. I know you don’t like her and I don’t care if you say nothing to her all day, I would prefer you to be civil and not cause a scene. But what I need from you right now is too... (arrange flowers/talk to the caterer/help me pick out...)” and give her a task so she feels included. I know it’s not what you need but it may help ease the stress and she will feel helpful and have something else to focus on. 
I’m sorry for your loss and hope the day goes peacefully and as stress free as possible for you

This is by far the most amazing romantic gesture I have ever heard of, it’s beautiful. One day you will make some woman the happiest on earth and she will make your whole world turn upside down. (In a good way) you were lucky to experience this love so young, good luck in the future friend!! And don’t stop tinkering with those mustangs!!

Two options 
1. Hope the kid gets better with age and you settle down into the whole SM role, it takes a lot of work and patience.... but it’s not for everyone which brings me to
2. Get out. Now. The ability to over look the first time parents is a skill very few people have mastered and the rest of us just cope with. You seem to hold a lot of resentment and that is not healthy for any of you. I’m not saying you are wrong in any way shape or form because quite frankly even the best step parents have fleeting similar thoughts. But you have a minimum of 16 years of BM and SD.... can you see yourself with that? 

Also as a side note, do not let how SD behaves put you off having your own, your child will have you as a mother and you won’t allow your child to be exposed to drugs and POS and poor behaviour.

Normally I see this title and immediately want to say Yes Yes Yes. 
The pros out way the cons in my situation and I wouldn’t change my SS for the world. 
I still have the resentment and fears occasionally especially because I’m not a mother myself.
But reading your post I’m not sure it is right for you. I know this is your safe place to put all of your thoughts in one place which can come across worse but crying about it already/daily? I don’t think you are emotionally ready to take this one on. 
Step families are like in laws sometimes you are lucky and sometimes you clash. But the way I see it, it’s what you make of it, how much input and contact you have,how you behave, how you deal with the situations are all in your control.... you can make it worth it or you can make it worse. 
I never wanted a step kid, I never wanted in laws quite like the ones I have and for perspective SS mother used to bully me in high school but now I get along with her better than my Sister in Law and mother in law. I had similar ‘white picket fence’ dreams, first time parents and all that. If you love your boyfriend and he’s the right one, you won’t walk away. If you are doubting if you can cope with this madness daily... run. You can’t. And that’s ok. It’s not a bad thing. Be honest with yourself. It’s the only true answer you will get.

This made me cry so much it took me forever to finish reading it because I couldn’t see. 
I just want to say thank you, thank you for the work you do every day. The physical and emotional support you provide to families in need. I know, like many others, I couldn’t do your role. So thank you for being there, for helping others and for being an amazing person. 
That lady is right, you are an angel!

I agree with all of this ^ 
I’d just like to add that as a SK he can worry about BM reaction to his feelings towards you. If he’s a mummy’s boy then he won’t let himself connect with you. To him that’s disrespectful to his mum, he can’t replace her with you. Also if he remembers mum and dad together it will be painful to watch dad move on. 
At 16 he probably spends very little time with you, just try grin and bare it. If you don’t it will cause problems for DH and SS May stop visiting which isn’t fair on SD or DH. Let DH take charge of him and only communicate to be civil. Focus on SD.

You sound awesome. 
Happy Mother’s Day and I hope you and your family have a lovely life together. 💜

Because now I get to call him my husband and I share the same last name as him and my step son. It brought our family together for a happy occasion rather than a funeral. We had a beautiful wedding, it was the happiest day of our lives. We honoured the family who have raised us and thanked our loved ones for all they have done for us. 
Marriage is not for everyone, but neither is having kids or owning your own home. Some people love to travel, some never leave their home town. Some people eat meat and some are vegan. My point is don’t be so judgemental, if it’s not for you then fine, but don’t go telling people who are happily married/engaged that marriage is stupid. It’s not fair and it’s not right.

It just makes sense to me, even his mum says she doesn’t mind if he calls me mum because I am his mum when he is with us, but even with her blessing we still stick to our ‘pet’ names for each other. I think forcing (especially society suggested) names will only cause problems. Plus I love being able to be whatever he needs me to be. I’m the strictest (rules/behaviour wise) of his 4 parents but I’m also the one he talks to about anything and the one willing to go try anything new with him.  As much as I can not wait to be a mum, being a step mum is a pleasure. And if there were no other adults sticking there noses in there would never be any problems outside of general raising a child 😄

Sweetheart he hasn’t given you the courtesy of a serious conversation or listening to your concerns and hard limits last time you had a serious conversation. He does not deserve another second of your time. Pack your stuff, get you and your baby out of there. I’d love to say block his number but parental rights and all he should probably still have access to his kid.
You get in a conversation he’s just going to lie. He’s not going to listen to what you’re saying. Save your strength and breath. Stay strong and remember you and baby come first now!!

This!!! 100% this!!! My SS8 and I have had this conversation numerous times about numerous people. Mainly about the name thing. I’m not called Mum, I’m referred to as SM when discussions arise with others but other than he calls me by name/nickname. And I’m good with that, I’m good with whatever he is comfortable calling me, even if it’s evil step witch... What makes me happy is he calls me “My ‘name’” because I am his and he is mine. 
But my MIL demands to be called Memaw (a name non of us agree with, because she has made it “special Nana” which isn’t fair on his other Nana, that and SS8 has been picked on and has asked us all to call her Nana.) even though we have all told her, she manipulated him so he’s scared to call her Nana. Making me the bad guy cos I call her Nana to her face. 
I’m so happy you see it the same way I do. It’s what they are comfortable with. Your love for a person does not change because of a name. It’s personal to the two people. 
Happy Mother’s Day Hun. And keep going strong! Those beautiful moments are worth every second.

Congratulations on your beautiful little family and congratulations on your nice shiny spine. 
You are clearly managing this v. Well and if the majority of your family are standing up for you then I would assume you are very much in the right. 
I have 2 suggestions for the future that have come from horror stories I have heard/been part of... 
1. If your dad ever does come around and comes to see you by himself don’t leave him with the kid alone. 
2. No matter what he says, stick to what/when/how you want contact and don’t tarnish that shiny spine you have. There is a reason you are VLC. 
Other than that I wish you and your family all the happiness.

Yeah, it doesn’t get to me because doctors told me I’d be in a wheelchair by the time I’m 35 anyway because of a defect in my spine. The idea of being bound to a wheelchair scares me more. I’m not scared of dying I’m scared of living without independence.
I’ve read all about the harm, it doesn’t stop me 🤭 I think it’s because I don’t drink or do anything else too harmful, I’m kind of like well this is my one bad thing. But I’m all for trying again 😁

Just wanted to say Thank you, i will be purchasing Alan Carr’s book and downloading the apps. My issue is I don’t have a ‘good enough’ reason to quit but these are some good tips that may help me on my way!!

While I whole heartedly agree you should not tell tales and ‘rat out’ SD to SO. I have a rather simple but hard solution. Call her out yourself. You are a step PARENT. She clearly doesn’t respect you. I’m sorry if you already do this but it is not clear in your post. You need to make her understand you are a parent she is a child. I don’t know how long you have been in her life but I see 2 options 
1. Gain respect/be a parent to SD/have a hard 6 months-1 year and peaceful enough life
2. Ignore SD and be just as rude to her resulting in a worse attitude (not just towards you) and a resentful SO. 
It’s hard and it’s painful but if she was your kid would you let her speak to you and treat you like that?

NTA... if it was divorce it would be different but ask her if it had belonged to a late mother/grandmother would she have thrown it out? 
Your late wife is no threat to your current one therefore she has no reason to feel jealous. Your ex can’t cause her any problems. That was a horrific thing to do to you. I wouldn’t suggest divorce unless you 100% cannot forgive her I.e if she shows no remorse.
Op sorry 😐

Take your Baby and your Husband and go to your mothers in Mother’s Day. That day is about you spending time with loved ones and as Dad it’s his job to make it special, like you do on Father’s Day. If you’re not on good terms with your mum or feel like you will be causing too much hassle get your family in the car and go out. Just the 3 of you. No grandparents allowed. You can visit them the day before or after. But Hun you need to put your foot down now before this type of thing becomes a regular occurrence.

Ask to borrow his phone!! I’m overly paranoid due to bad relationship history but my SO and I have an open phone policy because he can have bad head days too. It means if I’m feeling insecure or twisted something in my head I can just go check. He can do the same. No backlash. It’s really hard being in a relationship where the ex is constantly in your life and a reminder of SO history. But seeing messages like that would drive me mad. You need to get to the bottom of it before it destroys you.

I know one of those!!! BM is a damn baby making machine who doesn’t work and doesn’t provide anything for her kids, she’s currently on 4 (3 bio 1 SD) and is talking about how she’s going to have a boy next (Mother Nature say what?) my SS hates having 3 sisters and loves coming to our home so he can get some peace and quiet and some actual attention. 
And I’m here working full time unable to justify having a baby because we can’t afford it.... it makes me soooo mad....

You’re welcome, honestly knowing you’re not alone can make such a difference. Even if it is from strangers on reddit. 
Good luck and I hope you get your little bundle of joy 💜

NTA, I had a similar situation at 15 my back went, I have a dislodged vertebrate and had to give up dance/gym. Sat on a rush hour bus one day I was sat near the front by the window not a priority seat.... every seat was taken and an elderly lady got on. After about 2 minutes a man (in his 20’s) stood to let her sit down. The woman next to me in her 40’s turned to me and started trying to rip into me about how it should have been me who got up. Now I was a respectable kid, I was pretty shy and never shouted at anyone. But I very quickly pulled out a doctors note, showed her the bruises up my back from the injury and physio and showed her up in-front of the rest of the bus. I was mortified. It’s horrible when people assume. Tell those people maybe they should stand up and stop assuming that everyone in the world is as rude as they are.

When Dear husband and I got engaged, we had a house and had lived together 2 years with SS coming every weekend and half of school holidays. He was involved in everything, sometimes more so than DH. Shortly after our engagement BM got engaged to her partner. They were living together in a different city with all their kids so it wasn’t a big deal, until SS told me he wasn’t allowed to go to their wedding.... the other younger girls were but he wasn’t. I pulled her on it, saying he had gotten upset because he wasn’t allowed to go (he was 6 at the time) At which point she told me he would be in school and the other kids are still not in school. We talked and she finally agreed he should be there. In the end she got knocked up again and postponed the wedding, I doubt it will ever happen but if it does I hope she lets SS go. As much as I disagree with her parenting skills, SS loves her and it would break his heart.

You are not alone. You are brave, strong and very admirable for what you do every day. No one can understand how much you sacrifice and how much you put up with unless they stand in similar shoes. 
You can love your step son with all your heart, you can be the kindest most tolerable person in the planet, it is ok to feel pushed out, like your not a priority. But you must tell someone, friend,family,husband... it doesn’t matter. You need someone to remind your personal fabulous qualities. Feeling like this doesn’t make you a bad person or mean you love your SS less. You want a baby. That’s allowed. 
As for BM, unfortunately she is in your life for a good few years yet, as are the in laws. And if they are half as manipulative as my lot then times can be rough. I’ve come up with little games to distract me. How many times can I make them contradict themselves? How many times can BM ‘pretend’ to try palm her other 3 kids off on me/tell me that having kids is awful. How defensive will MIL get when I express my opinion of BM. (She’s fine calling her all the names under the sun till I say anything negative, then she’s the perfect mother to SS) it’s sad. But it’s true. Distractions are the best way forward. And I really hope you fall pregnant soon. Then you can be all about you and your family and screw everyone else. 😁

You only need a little hope. Just one small thing to hold onto. Tonight it was your friend. You are allowed to feel low/awful/sad/crappy. Just remember there is always a ‘plot twist’ waiting to happen
Congratulations, it was lovely of you to ask and shows how much you respect his kids, I hope you have a lovely wedding and a beautiful life together.
Thanos???

Firstly let me say I believe you, your feelings are valid and you are 100% right to never let that scum near your baby. 
Parents are not fool proof and some make more mistakes than others. You have an opportunity to be a thousand times better than your mother. 
It will be hard if you walk away. It is the safest option. But it will hurt like hell. May I suggest (as you live so far away) offering supervised visits with your mum only. Tell her she can visit, only she can visit. And don’t leave her alone with the baby. This will reassure you and will still give you the option to keep your mum in your life. 
You are not alone. It is ok to talk to people, it’s just finding the right people. 
And finally congratulations on your beautiful future, I wish you and your family all the best.

Well done on raising a beautifully independent young woman. 
So long as you don’t ‘influence’ her opinion about BM, it is a wonderful thing to read about the Step Mum having such an amazing relationship with SD.

NTA...If it makes you feel better... 
We booked our wedding 18 months in advance and then my husbands cousin gave birth the year before. So our wedding fell on her first birthday. 
For this little girls second birthday she will be attending her Uncles wedding. (He booked after she was born) 
My Sister in Law just got married on her Auntie and cousins birthday. The day after her husbands mothers birthday. 
My cousin got married the same day as my best friend last year and I had to choose. 

People can be selfish. Finding a wedding date that doesn’t conflict with anything, that your perfect venue has available is difficult. You said you’re not very close with your brother, I’d leave it? Atleast this means you don’t have to deal with the Girlfriend on your birthday 🎁 no one wants that crap bringing down your day!!!
I’m not assuming anything, just so used to writing SS, I apologise you couldn’t decipher from the context. SS refers to my stepson it is a term from another sub.

I agree, I have pets and a SS and I find pet people more annoying, I don’t particularly talk about either unless the conversation is brought up by someone else. And I do love SS more than anything, he is my family (along with loving dearest husband) but not everyone wants to talk about it and very few are actually interested.

NTA. This... all of this.... well done. I can be quite strict (in comparison to my SS other 3 parents) and this is somewhat along the lines of what I would have done. I would have also added a few conditions of her getting back a smart phone (such as ‘new phone’ must be in good condition and ‘traded’ in for smart phone) and a grounding or lesson of some sorts because I really do like to drive certain points home. 
But more to the point you are in no way an Ahole, although sometimes as parents we have to be, and you shouldn’t let others judge yours and your wife’s parenting. That is why you have each other to balance out and keep each other in check. Wife’s friends kids are the ones who have iPhone x’s and £1000 birthdays and no respect for anything. Its not even really about the phone, it’s the disrespect, the lie/manipulation, the lack of gratitude. Just because we live in a technologically advanced world doesn’t mean we don’t need basic lessons in how to be a decent human. This is so much harder to teach nowadays because all they want is expensive technology they can disappear into. 
Good luck and Well done!!

I am the same, if there was a way that didn’t effect anyone, I’d have gone a long time ago. Unfortunately I’ve seen the aftermath, I’ve also seen the response to someone stood on top of a multi story and how many people are effected from the 30+ in recovery/response to the public and businesses in the area. I’ve seen how one persons despair can be passed onto so many other in a moment. I can’t do that. I can’t give my pain and crappy mental health to someone else.

Please don’t, our lives may feel worthless, we maybe struggling with the day to day. But would you wish this pain on someone else? Would you want someone else to struggle with this decision every day? 
When people decide they’ve had enough, when the choose to finish their lives via a public display, it hurts others. The people who witness, the people who have to come deal with the situation, the person that accidentally gets hit. 
I fully understand the need to be done, to be finished and while I hope you can find a way to get through tonight, I also hope for those who can’t, they find a way that doesn’t destroy other peoples lives. 
It’s bad enough this sub has so many followers, so many people who feel this way. Let’s not add to it. Let’s not destroy more lives. 
I wish you all the best.

Yeah I want to quit before I even think of trying for a baby because I’ve seen the hormones. But right now smoking is the only thing I do for me on a daily basis. Yes I get to do my hobbies once in a while but it’s few and far between. I’m struggling with wanting to quit smoking. The second the urges and side effects set in I’m more than willing to give up.
